## What we got from our local land grant

As a farm family, we got many useful things from Virginia Tech and its
extension service: 

- Evidence basis and demonstration of best practices
- Documents that provided guidance: "helpfiles"
- Recipes!
- Training to make the best, safest use of available tools

Overall, we got information and training that was **based on good science**, **free**, 
**practical**, and ready to **use right away**.

## Assessing exposure

\begin{block}{Challenge for epidemiological research}
How can we determine whether a county was exposed to a tropical storm, in a 
way that is consistent over many storms in many places over many years?
\end{block}

Previous approaches have varied but include: 

- Distance from storm track
- Storm winds above a threshold
- Evacuation orders
- FEMA reports
- Combined metric (property damage, power outages, gas shortages, etc.)

## `hurricaneexposure` package

\footnotesize
\begin{block}{`hurricaneexposure` package}
\medskip
Create county-level exposure time series for tropical storms in U.S. counties. Exposure can be determined based on several hazards (e.g., wind, rain, tornadoes), with user-specified thresholds. 
\end{block}

\bigskip

```{r echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
county_wind(counties = c("22071", "51700"), wind_limit = 21, 
            start_year = 1995, end_year = 2005)
```

```{r echo = FALSE}
county_wind(counties = c("22071", "51700"), wind_limit = 21, 
            start_year = 1995, end_year = 2005) %>%
  slice(1:4) %>%
  select(storm_id, fips, closest_date, vmax_sust)
```

```{r frances_rain_example, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4, fig.align = "center", out.width = "0.9\\textwidth", warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}

map_tracks(storms = storm, plot_points = FALSE, 
                plot_object = map_counties(storm = storm, 
                                           metric = "rainfall")) + 
        ggtitle("Rainfall during Frances, 2004")
```

## Project software

\footnotesize
\begin{block}{`stormwindmodel`}
Model storm winds from Best Tracks data at U.S. locations. Includes modeling sustained and gust winds, as well as duration of sustained and gust winds above a specified threshold. 
\end{block}

\footnotesize
\begin{block}{`noaastormevents`}
Download and explore listings from the NOAA Storm Events database. Includes the ability to pull events based on a tropical storm, using events listed close in time and distance to the storm's tracks. 
\end{block}

\footnotesize
\begin{block}{`countytimezones`}
Convert time-stamps from UTC to local time zones for U.S. counties based on county FIPs. Facilitates merging weather observations with locally measured data, including health outcomes.
\end{block}

\footnotesize
\begin{block}{`weathermetrics`}
Functions to convert between weather metrics, including conversions for metrics of temperature, air moisture, wind speed, and precipitation. This package also includes functions to calculate the heat index.
\end{block}

\footnotesize
\begin{block}{`weathermetrics`}
Functions to convert between weather metrics, including conversions for metrics of temperature, air moisture, wind speed, and precipitation. This package also includes functions to calculate the heat index.
\end{block}

## Sharing data through an R package

1. Data access is **scripted**---easy to reproduce and adapt later.
2. Dataset is **versioned**---the version of the data package changes
as the dataset is updated. The version number can be included as part
of Methods section of studies.
3. Data can be **easily integrated** with other tools available through R.
These include mapping and statistical tools.
4. Data creation is **documented and reproducible** on GitHub
starting from public data and software.

# Teach

## ERHS 535---R Programming for Research

- "In-depth instruction on data collection, data management, programming, 
and visualization, using data examples relevant to academic research."
- Flipped classroom, in-person time focuses on applied group coding exercises
- Project-based, final group project develops a web-based interactive data
visualization

## ERHS 535---R Programming for Research

R Programming for Research (ERHS 535) has been taken by students pursuing 
degrees in: 

Environmental Health, Cellular \& Molecular Biology, 
Public Health, Microbiology, Clinical Sciences, Animal Sciences, 
Mechanical Engineering, Ecology, Radiological Health Sciences, 
Biochemistry, Food Science \& Nutrition, Pathology, 
Human Development \& Family Studies, Civil \& Environmental Engineering, 
Ecosystem Sustainability, Fish Wildlife and Conservation Biology, 
Forest Sciences, Soil \& Crop Sciences, Chemical Engineering, Horticulture, 
Data Analysis, Civil Engineering, Mathematics, and Chemistry
